Rule 14 aligns the waw where the ASV writes a connective for it; every circumstantial waw so aligned in this chapter takes a clause-initial subordinator (v. 29 "when"). Here the ASV subordinates with the participle "being", which rule 20 assigns to the predicate, leaving the waw no word of its own, as at 1KI.19.19. Aligning it to "yet" instead remains defensible.
Verbless clause: the supplied copula "being" joins the predicate it licenses, and "a" belongs to the noun.

This "yet" is temporal "still", not the adversative connective rule 14 would put on the waw, and it stands inside the clause after the copula rather than at its edge. The sense is עוֹד's elsewhere (1KI.1.14, 1KI.1.22) and no such morpheme is present, so nothing licenses it; the waw's circumstantial force is already spent on "being" under rule 20. Reading it as the waw's rendering remains defensible.

Where the ASV does write a second word — a widow woman at 1 Ki 17:9 — rule 30's condition is unmet and rule 2 would split it. Rules 2/30/33: ever jointly renders the comprehensive duration of all days; for supplies the temporal accusative relation of that expression. Giving for to kol would assign a duration helper as if it independently rendered the quantifier, while leaving kol unrepresented would discard the totality carried inside ever. Retain the two lexical morphemes fused, headed on the temporal noun and ever; the article contributes no English determination and stands separately unrepresented.
Rules 29/30: for ever writes no determiner realizing the article; a fixed expression does not absorb an article whose sense its English rendering does not carry.
